method.retry: Visible DEPLOY AGAIN button after attempt 1; no third deployment.
method.observation: Visible game screenshots inspected using view_image, plus driver-returned visible UI text and own action timing evidence. No source, tests, internal game state, earlier reviews, solutions, test URLs, arbitrary game evaluation, or shared preview browser used.
method.tactics: Attempt 1 opened with an aimed rifle burst, detoured toward West Archive, recovered West/Heart/East, and approached the Custodian. Attempt 2 opened with the pump breacher, recovered Heart/West/East, used rifle optic shots, then flanked into the Custodian hall and disabled two coils.
confounds: Browser-timed synthetic DOM input through ordinary listeners; this is paused synthetic play, not a human continuous session.
Batches capture after actions. Most batches automatically Escape-paused; resume used the visible Resume button. This grants substantial planning time.

Several early actions were chosen from the preceding photograph while the next image was being requested, so view-dependent decisions lagged by one photograph. Later alignment photographs were inspected separately before acting. Moving targets, stale views and my corrections contributed to misses; these are not attributed to game aiming bugs.

Screenshot scheduling and browser performance time add delay. A nominal 100 ms fire hold sometimes lasted about 130-192 ms in recorded browser timings; screenshot captures commonly took roughly 160-340 ms.
Held ADS captures used captureHeld and explicitly released firing/movement first in many cases; held ADS photographs still leave aim held during capture. Default captures release controls first.
Fallback look used the right mouse button held. Short settling waits were generally used before captures, but some movement/reload photographs capture a transient state.
One relative look request of -2450 was rejected as Invalid relative mouse delta (sequence 29). It was preserved and followed with a valid -2400 request; no mission reset occurred.
Software-WebGL fallback was enabled; no hardware, framerate, latency, audio quality, or human enjoyment certification is claimed.

attempts.summary: The opening rifle ADS burst visibly produced WARDEN // CRITICAL +180. Many later shots missed, including firing at walls or empty lanes after stale-view turns. Low cover and archive wall detours consumed much of the run. Recovered all cores, reached the Custodian exterior without a clear coil line, and died during a south/west flank and reload.
honestFailures: Repeated cover collisions and wall-facing movement.
Breacher shots often missed; cannot infer its damage balance from this run.
Some long bursts were fired without a visible target at the final aim point.
Heart recovery was tried too far away before moving into its floor ring.
Custodian firing line was never established.

attempts.summary: Pump breacher eliminated the opening Warden after several shots and corrections. Reload showed individual Shell seated messages. Recovered Heart first; rifle realignment on its Warden produced the second elimination. Repeated north-wall detours preceded West recovery. Crossed the yard to East, then entered the Custodian hall. Rifle bursts disabled coils 3 and 2. Health fell to 6 while stationary firing with nearby sentinels; a final Shift/reload/strafe attempt ended in death before the remaining coil was disabled.
honestFailures: Early breacher shots and a yard burst missed.
Several navigation batches still ran into archive walls or took the wrong route.
Stationary coil firing left me exposed; the final loss is not proof that the encounter is impossible or unfair.

weaponHandMaterialHandling.rifle: Dark slate-blue angular receiver, squared open optic frame, cyan accent strip and simple beveled surfaces. ADS clearly centers and enlarges the weapon. The initial optic burst killed a Warden and later aligned fire killed the Heart Warden. Rifle reload showed a repositioned lower hand and a Reloading/Weapon ready state; ammo and reserve updated. Sustained fire and reload were exercised.
weaponHandMaterialHandling.breacher: Chunkier, long flat top and two bright gold/yellow front sight posts; plainly distinguishable from the rifle. Single trigger presses consumed shells, with visible delays/cadence between shots. Attempt 2 neutralized the opening Warden. Reload produced separate Shell seated messages and reached six shells. No claim of spread or exact damage values is supported.
weaponHandMaterialHandling.hands: Gray-blue gloves and sleeves are visible at the supporting grip, with segmented/ribbed finger shapes and a lower gripping hand during rifle reload. They read as simplified faceted models. Still photographs do not support a full animation or anatomical rigging audit.
weaponHandMaterialHandling.materials: Weapons and gloves mostly use clean broad surfaces with restrained bevel highlights; limited visible fine wear, seams, fabric grain, or complex metal variation. Rain, wet floor reflections, cracked concrete and warm/cyan lights give the environment more surface variety than the first-person assets.
handlingCoverage: Rifle hip and ADS views, sustained fire, reload, swap.
Breacher hip and ADS views, multiple deliberate shots, reload.
Sprint, movement, Shift, Space attempt, Tab hold and paused facility map.
limits: No comprehensive recoil, reload interruption, damage, precision, animation continuity or performance measurement.
Space was tried and vault prompts were seen, but screenshots do not prove a full successful vault sequence.
Tab was held for photographs; a reliable ground-trace route was not established in the captured views.
Shift produced PHASE BREAK / DISCHARGE CANCELED once, while both terminal scorecards reported zero phase evades.

strengths.finding: Cohesive rainy industrial setting with cyan highlights, warm pools of light and reflected floor lighting; the title screen establishes a clear visual identity.
Warden optic/amber charge and contextual Shift-or-optic prompts are visually distinct. An aligned opening rifle burst gave clear critical feedback.
Map names objectives and distinguishes wall, low cover, receiver and player. Core recovery floor-ring prompts, memory cards and restored supplies communicate progress.
Custodian UI communicates armored/open states and individual OFF coils. Clear rifle fire visibly disabled two coils, making progress readable.
End screens show recovered people, eliminations, time, score, accuracy and a direct visible retry.

defectsAndFriction.finding: Near walls, large scenery surfaces occlude most of the view and the weapon disappears substantially into/behind the surface. This hinders orientation and first-person presentation. Repeated independent examples occurred around archive and Custodian walls; collision internals were not inspected.

Navigating around archive walls and low cover repeatedly required corrections. World hints identify south intake/east service, but a direct objective marker can remain across blocked geometry and the hinted opening took effort to find. My stale-view controls and route mistakes materially contribute to this result.

First-person weapons, hands and sentinels retain broad, simple geometry and clean materials. They communicate function, but the close view lacks the surface richness and model detail expected of a finished AAA presentation.
Some contextual copy, map legends and weapon status labels are very small at the captured 1280 by 800 presentation; reading them requires close inspection.

Health fell rapidly during exposed Custodian firing while close sentinels were present. Directional orange indicators existed, but paused stills did not establish which source dealt each hit. This limits combat-source readability assessment and is not a verified damage or fairness defect.

ratings.scale: 0-10, higher is better; subjective assessment of observed slice under this method.

gameplay.reason: Functional recovery/combat loop, alternate core order, supplies and a multi-component final fight. Route friction and exposure cost were substantial, with control confounds acknowledged.

presentation.reason: Strong coherent menu, lighting and wet industrial atmosphere; first-person and enemy assets remain visibly simple and close-wall occlusion reduces polish.

usability.reason: Useful map, interaction ring instructions, status feedback and retry. Small text and obstructed objective approaches took effort to resolve.

combatReadability.reason: Optics, amber charges, critical feed and coil OFF states are clear. Threat-source attribution in close multi-enemy fighting was less clear in stills.

aaaReadiness.reason: A coherent playable slice with working mission progression, but visual asset detail, near-wall weapon behavior and the unverified animation/audio/performance/extraction coverage prevent a finished AAA judgment.

coverageLimits: Exactly two ordinary terminal losses; no win, extraction upload, full memory-reading screen or settings flow evaluated.
No bugs inferred from source or tests; no runtime changes made.
No human enjoyment, audio, hardware, accessibility compliance, or broad platform certification claimed.
Low accuracy in attempt 1 is explicitly preserved and substantially reflects reviewer tactics and delayed photographs.

pidVerification.meaning: Neither exact owned PID was present after driver exit.
